contributions.who: The Secretary of State for Education (Lucy Powell)
contributions.text: Today I am publishing the Government’s response to the independent review of antisemitism in schools and colleges in England, led by Sir David Bell. Sir David’s review presents a stark and timely warning. It finds that antisemitism is a significant and growing problem in modern Britain, and that Jewish pupils, students and staff are increasingly experiencing its consequences. It concludes that antisemitism is a distinct form of racism that requires a clear and specific response, and that our schools and colleges have a critical role to play in challenging prejudice and preventing hatred from becoming normalised. I am pleased to confirm that the Government have accepted all 27 of Sir David’s recommendations. This represents a significant and long-term commitment to ensuring that every school and college is equipped to identify, challenge and prevent antisemitism. Jewish children, young people and staff should be able to learn and work in safety, free from prejudice, intimidation and discrimination. That must be a basic expectation in every education setting.
